answer: To hold k identities, an operator's oldest identity must lock k cubed attested epochs of its own tenure; the first locks one, the tenth 1,000, the thousandth 1,000,000,000, and locked epochs never count again. A wander that starts at the last admitted identity's jetty and is signed at the oasis extends that same oldest ledger; the oasis signs only a wander continuous from the last berth, so a new address cannot begin a second ledger.
